Jordan — great, appreciate the clarifications. Attached is the short runbook and a proposed pass/fail criteria table embedded in the POC spreadsheet. High level:

Test plan (short):
- Streaming behavior: replay your sample requests against a streaming endpoint. Check: chunk boundaries, token order, and ability to recover schema when messages are split. Pass = >= 98% messages fully valid after reassembly; fail threshold < 95%.

Subject: Re: Redwood feature parity tests — quick notes on differentiation and test hooks

Jordan / Marissa — quick note from the product side to help calibrate the live run. A few differentiators to watch for during the tests and some practical hooks we propose for the function-calling pass/fail logic:

Differentiators to observe:
- Deterministic reassembly: our streaming runtime attaches chunk-sequence metadata and optional resumable tokens so your client can reliably reassemble split structured outputs (helps with your corner-case).
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated multi-turn calls (your 2k token cases), KV caching avoids repeated compute on static prefixes which reduces p95 latency by ~25% in similar workloads.
- Fallback routing: if a dedicated model variant is overloaded, requests will automatically route to a compatible quantized variant — measurable in the test by intentional throttling.

Suggested test hooks (we'll provide CLI helpers):
1) For function calls: include a request-id header and have Redwood return a call-status field in the response. We'll treat a function call as \"successful\" if final_status==\"success\" and side-effects (webhook) were triggered exactly once. We'll run retries and verify idempotency.
2) For streaming: add a chunk-seq header; our SDK will output chunk metadata which you can assert against. We'll include a small Node/py snippet in the runbook.
3) For structured outputs: we'll run JSON-schema validation after reassembly and after retry to ensure determinism.

I'll attach the quick-run snippets to the invite. If you want to test dedicated capacity, we can schedule a ramp window after the basic POC.

—Rishi
